title: Going somewhere
description: Talk about leaving, arriving, and the journey.
grammar: the verb ir in the present
grammarNote: Ir is irregular: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van.

explanation.summary: Ir means to go, and it is one of the most irregular verbs in Spanish. It is also the verb that carries almost all of the near future, which is why it matters more than it looks.

sections.heading: The forms
sections.body: Only the nosotros and vosotros forms are regular: vamos, vais. The rest are irregular: voy, vas, va, van. The word for the place goes after a, not de: voy a la playa, vas al trabajo.

sections.heading: Going to somewhere, going to do something
sections.body: Two patterns that look alike. Ir + a + a place says where you are going: voy a Madrid. Ir + a + an infinitive says what you are going to do: voy a estudiar. The difference is what follows the a: a place, or a verb.

sections.heading: Coming and going
sections.body: Volver is to come back, and it is irregular in the yo form: vuelvo. Salir is to leave or to go out, and it is irregular: salgo. And ir and venir are opposites that do not need a preposition between them: ir y venir.

examples.es: Voy y vengo en el día.
examples.en: I go and come during the day.
